title: Why Skilled Nursing Shouldn't Use General Asset Software
summary: Why general asset-tracking software fails in skilled nursing: it depends on scanning and lacks SNF-native, room-level, survey-ready equipment tracking.
body_text: Skilled nursing facilities should not run their equipment on general asset-tracking software, because those tools are built to catalog IT gear, fixed assets, or maintenance work, and they only know where something is when a human scans it. A nursing floor needs automatic room-level location and durable-medical-equipment workflows, which is a purpose-built job. Below is the honest breakdown, including where the general tools genuinely earn their place. The equipment question in a nursing home is really a margin question. A typical 110-bed skilled nursing facility loses $155,000 to $500,000 a year to equipment waste: rentals that keep billing past their return date, owned wheelchairs and pumps nobody can find, and duplicate purchases of gear already sitting in a closet one floor up. The median skilled nursing facility runs on a 1.8% operating margin , so equipment waste alone can equal or exceed everything the building earns in a year. We break that cost model down in the 2026 SNF equipment waste report . Whatever tool you choose has to move that number, not just produce a tidier list. What general asset software actually is The tools that come up in this search are all well-built, and they are all general-purpose. It helps to say plainly what each one is for. Sortly is a visual inventory app for small businesses. Photo-based records, custom fields and folders, barcode and QR scanning, and low-stock and maintenance-date alerts. It is genuinely good for a small team that wants a flexible, searchable list of supplies, tools, or equipment. Snipe-IT is a free, open-source IT asset manager. It tracks who has which laptop, license, and peripheral, with strong audit logging and a clean REST API. For an IT department on a budget, it is a well-loved choice. EZOfficeInventory (EZO) is a broader enterprise asset and maintenance platform used across many industries. It handles asset lifecycle, check-in and check-out, maintenance scheduling, and barcode or RFID verification, with role-based permissions for larger teams. Wasp AssetCloud is fixed-asset tracking built around barcode and RFID. Its strength is fast, accurate audits: RFID lets you sweep many tags at once instead of scanning one by one, which is a real advantage at inventory time. UpKeep is a mobile-first CMMS (computerized maintenance management system). Work orders, preventive maintenance, and asset records built for maintenance technicians in the field. It is a strong maintenance tool. The honest credit: every one of these does its intended job well, and several are cheaper on day one than a purpose-built system. If your requirement is a flexible catalog of assets that rarely move, or a maintenance backlog to work through, one of them is a reasonable buy. Why the general model breaks on a nursing floor The catch is structural, and it is not a knock on the software. Every tool above shares one assumption: an item's location is whatever a person last recorded. Sortly and Snipe-IT update on a scan or a check-out. EZOfficeInventory updates on a scan or check-in. Wasp updates on a scan cycle, even a fast RFID one. UpKeep tracks an assigned-location field a technician edits. In all of them, the map is exactly as accurate as staff discipline: every item, every move, forever. That assumption holds in a warehouse or an IT stockroom, where assets sit still and one person owns the record. It does not hold on a nursing floor. Equipment moves constantly, no one is assigned to log the moves, and the staff who would do the scanning already lose 30 to 60 minutes per shift hunting for gear. Asking them to stop and scan a wheelchair every time it rolls to a new room is added work during the exact moments they have none to spare. Within a few weeks the database drifts from reality, and a location record you cannot trust is one people stop opening. This is why zero-scanning, automatic tracking is the requirement that separates SNF-fit tools from the rest. Drift is also where the money hides. The single largest equipment leak in skilled nursing is rentals that should have gone back: a facility keeps paying a daily rate on a specialty mattress or a therapy pump long after it is needed, because nobody can confirm the unit is sitting unused in a storage room. A scan-based catalog cannot catch that, because the catch depends on knowing the live location and status of every billable item without asking anyone to do anything. The three things a SNF needs that general tools do not carry 1. Automatic room-level location. Not sub-meter precision, and not "last scanned in the east wing three days ago." The floor needs to know which room an item is in right now, updated on its own. That is the difference between a records system and a location system. 2. Durable-medical-equipment economics. Rental elimination, duplicate-purchase prevention, and cross-facility sharing are workflows, not fields. They only run when the location data is live and trustworthy. A general catalog has no rental engine because it has no live location to trigger one. 3. Survey readiness. Equipment that cannot be located, or that is out of service, surfaces in the annual survey. The most-cited deficiency on standard nursing-home surveys is F689 , the accident-hazards and supervision tag, cited on roughly a quarter of standard surveys. A one-click, always-current equipment audit report is a SNF-native feature. Exporting a spreadsheet from an IT asset tool is not the same thing. The honest comparison Tool Built for Location method Staff scanning SNF-native workflows Norra Skilled nursing DME Room-level, automatic, always current None Purpose-built for skilled nursing Sortly Small-business visual inventory Last scan only ❌ Every item, every move ❌ General-purpose ❌ Snipe-IT IT hardware and licenses Last check-out record ❌ Manual entry or scan ❌ General-purpose ❌ EZOfficeInventory Multi-industry asset lifecycle Last scan or check-in ❌ Every move ❌ General-purpose ❌ Wasp AssetCloud Fixed-asset audits Last scan, batch RFID ❌ Scan cycles ❌ General-purpose ❌ UpKeep Maintenance work orders Assigned-location field ❌ Manual update ❌ Maintenance, not location ❌ Read the table fairly. The general tools are not badly made, and each wins for its own buyer: Snipe-IT is free and open-source for IT teams, Sortly is the simplest flexible catalog for a small team, Wasp does the fastest fixed-asset audits, EZOfficeInventory scales across many industries, and UpKeep is a genuinely strong maintenance system. What none of them was built to do is keep a live, trustworthy map of medical equipment on a floor where nobody has time to scan. That is the one axis that decides whether a nursing home keeps its money. Where Norra fits Norra is the AI equipment manager purpose-built for skilled nursing. Proprietary smart tags with multi-year battery life report room-level location through plug-in gateways, so there is no wiring, no infrastructure buildout, and no six-figure install. Staff never scan anything. The tags report location automatically, so the rental-elimination, loss-prevention, and cross-facility-sharing workflows run on live data instead of on whoever remembered to scan. Norra is a MatrixCare marketplace partner with a live integration, works alongside any EHR, and is backed by Y Combinator. Across a multi-facility skilled nursing network, it cut equipment spending by as much as 70 percent, drove 90 percent fewer new rental orders per month, saved over 1,100 staff hours a year, and brought unnecessary rentals to zero. It does all of this at a fraction of the cost of traditional hospital-grade tracking. None of that makes the general tools wrong. It makes them the wrong tool for this one job. If you also run IT hardware or a maintenance backlog, keep the tool that does it well. For the durable medical equipment that drives your margin, use a system built for the floor. For the wider field, including hospital-grade location systems and other SNF options, see our best equipment tracking systems for skilled nursing roundup and the buyer's guide for nursing homes . The bottom line Use a general asset tool if your assets sit still, one person owns the record, and your requirement is a flexible catalog or a maintenance queue. Sortly, Snipe-IT, EZOfficeInventory, Wasp, and UpKeep each do that job at a low starting cost. Use a SNF-native system if your equipment moves, your staff are busy, and the number that matters is equipment waste, not inventory tidiness. That means automatic room-level location, no scanning, rental elimination, and survey-ready reports. For a nursing home, the deciding condition is whether your equipment moves and your staff are busy. If both are true, a scan-based catalog will drift, and the rentals you are trying to catch are exactly what slips through. To see your own equipment on a live map instead, start with a single-facility pilot at norra.io .

title: How Much of Your Patent Practice Should You Codify?
summary: AI changes the payoff for codifying how your team drafts and reviews patents. Decide how much to codify yourself versus leave to a purpose-built platform.
body_text: Key takeaways • AI has raised the payoff for codifying patent practice. Codification now guides AI-assisted drafting and review directly, not just junior training. • A purpose-built patent platform can encode a large body of best practice out of the box, so a team can begin with that foundation rather than write its own. • Solve Intelligence maintains its shared foundation across more than 700 IP teams, keeping it current far more efficiently than any single team could alone. • The strategic choice is how much of your own practice to codify on top; scarce expert time should go to the standards and judgment that differentiate your work. • A named professional still signs off on every filing, so accountability for the result never shifts to the AI. Why clear standards drive quality and consistency At IP Counsel Cafe 2026, practitioners broadly agreed that the nearer-term shift is less about work allocation and more about how in-house teams and outside counsel work together, with clearer standards, higher quality, and more consistency on both sides. The common thread is how the work gets specified. Getting higher quality and efficiency from AI means stating clearly what good work looks like in a form a tool can apply and review. That is codification, and it matters far more now than it used to. None of this assumes AI is close to replacing professional judgment. Reasonable practitioners disagree about how capable it will become, and many doubt it will match seasoned judgment for years. The case for writing practice down does not rest on any forecast about AI. It rests on something already visible, namely that today's systems can follow clear instructions that reflect how strong work gets done. Why patent teams have rarely written down substantive standards Patent work has long run on expertise that is easier to exercise than to write down. An experienced practitioner knows how to structure a claim set , where a specification needs depth because of how prosecution tends to unfold, and when an office action calls for argument rather than amendment. The same holds for in-house and outside counsel alike. Many teams keep procedural checklists for filing and docketing, but substantive know-how tends to remain with individual practitioners or in their work product. Junior practitioners often have to learn from those sources. There are understandable reasons for this tendency. Until recently, writing down an approach to substantive issues offered a modest return, mainly greater consistency and better training materials. The effort also competed directly with billable work or other higher-priority tasks. Substantive practice also resists easy organization, since substantive judgment depends on the technical field, the jurisdiction, business strategy, and a body of law that keeps changing, often at once. Seen that way, not investing heavily in writing it all down may have been a reasonable choice. Take the drafting of a set of claims for a complex genus. No written rule tells you how many dependent claims to spin out, yet the total has to stay manageable rather than mechanically calling out every alternative in its own dependent claim. Over time, a practitioner develops a feel for it, promoting the alternatives that matter, such as those covering the exemplified or commercially significant embodiments, and folding the rest together. That feel is genuine expertise, and it usually stays unwritten. The moment you try to tell an AI how to draft those claims, you have to put into words the unspoken heuristics you had been applying. What AI changed, and what it didn't AI has changed the payoff for codifying practice. A codified standard used to do its work only when a colleague read it. Now the same standard can guide AI-assisted drafting on new matters and inform the review of the drafts that come back, across a whole portfolio. In effect, one practitioner's hard-won expertise, once codified, can raise the drafting and review of an entire team rather than staying locked in one person's matters. Codified practice has gone from a training aid to something that shapes output directly at scale. What AI has not changed is who is in control. The practitioner, not the tool, keeps the final call. The same holds for accountability. A named professional still signs off on the filing and stands behind it, whatever tools produced the draft. The judgment that shapes the result therefore stays human, even when the drafting is shared with a machine. This is where the tool itself matters. Solve Intelligence is designed to keep the practitioner in command, with clear visibility into what the AI produces at each step, the rationale shown alongside it, and control over the output. Used this way, codification extends an expert's reach across a portfolio and leaves more of their time for the highest-level decisions, which stay firmly with them. Build the foundation yourself, or use a platform? Anyone who uses AI at all builds on some foundation, and the question is how much of it a team supplies itself. A purpose-built platform can provide the out-of-the-box codification of best practice, along with patent data and tooling. It can also keep that foundation current as models, the law, and practice change. That work is substantial and never finished. Much of it does not set one team apart, so building it yourself consumes scarce time that could go toward what does. The more of the foundation a team starts with, the more of its remaining time goes to its own codification and judgment. A frontier model on its own gives you a thin foundation. It is a genuine starting point, but a general one. On a given matter, it may not reliably reflect current practice in a specific office or jurisdiction. It has no reliable access to patent data such as prior art and litigation history. It has no native support for figures, chemical structures, or sequence listings, and it is not maintained specifically for patent-practice accuracy. A team that starts there is choosing to supply the patent layer itself. A platform like Solve Intelligence supplies far more of that foundation. It sits on top of the same frontier models and adds the patent layer. Patent professionals build and maintain that layer, so a great deal of best practice is already encoded out of the box and a team starts from a higher baseline. Because that foundation is shared across more than 700 IP teams, it is kept current far more efficiently than any single team could manage alone. That foundation shows up in concrete features. Auto Template, available in Solve’s Drafting, Prosecution, and Charts products, turns a team's existing filings and internal standards into custom templates, so a team's own codification starts from real work rather than a blank page. That higher-level codification stays with the team. Solve Intelligence gives it a private, maintained place to encode and apply its custom templates and instructions, and the team decides how much of its judgment to write down and how much to keep in its people's hands. Where a team wants help capturing its own practice as standards, Solve's practitioners can assist, while the substantive choices and control over confidentiality remain with the team. The LexisNexis integration brings global patent litigation data into Solve’s drafting, prosecution, and claim-charting workflows, so the standards a team codifies and its everyday decisions can draw on current data. How much should you codify yourself? A good place to start is with what the purpose-built platform already provides. Because it encodes a great deal of common best practice, a team can use that foundation and apply practitioner judgment case by case without adding its own codification. That may be the right approach for some teams. Others may benefit from codifying distinctive aspects of their practice so the team can apply them consistently. The right level depends on each team's circumstances, priorities, and strategy. Custom guidance also takes work to build and keep current. A team should therefore add it where the expected gains in quality or consistency justify that effort, then revisit the choice as its practice, the law, and the technology change. When a team does add its own codification, a custom application template or a reusable house style is a common place to start. The larger decision is how far beyond that to go, toward the higher-level standards that carry more of a team's judgment and need more upkeep. An outside counsel team, for instance, might codify how it structures claims and specifications to withstand validity challenges it encounters repeatedly in its field. An in-house team might codify what a specification has to cover for its own products and standards, so every outside firm starts from the same baseline. These choices do more than shape each side's internal practice. They also affect how in-house teams and outside counsel divide and coordinate the work. An in-house team might codify enough to review incoming drafts or give outside counsel a structured starting point. Outside counsel might use its own standards to produce more consistent work across matters while keeping higher-level strategy in its lawyers' judgment. Neither side has a settled playbook, and the right balance will continue to evolve. With the shared foundation handled, both sides can put the time they save toward better work. That may mean sharper strategic judgment, additional codification, or both. Where to start Start with a strong, well-maintained foundation rather than rebuilding one yourself. Then treat how much of your own to codify as an ongoing experiment, not a fixed formula. For in-house teams, the near-term step may be to add only the codification with a clear payoff and reassess how much further to go. That includes deciding what to build internally and what to leave to the platform or outside counsel. For outside counsel, codifying a practice's expertise turns it into something the firm can demonstrate and retain. Keeping those standards sound as the law develops is exactly the kind of judgment that stays valuable. For both, the strategic move is to put scarce effort into the codification and judgment that differentiate the work, and to let a purpose-built platform carry the foundation. Solve Intelligence is built for either side of the table. A law firm can hold its own codification on the platform as its asset, and an in-house team can maintain and refine its standards there. But codification is not the only thing that stays with the team. However the work is divided, and however much is handed to the tool, the responsibility for the result does not move. That is why the judgment behind the standards remains the practitioner's to own. title: 50 Must-Know Revit Shortcuts for Architects {{year}}
summary: Learn the most useful Revit shortcuts for architects and BIM professionals to navigate projects faster, improve efficiency, and reduce repetitive tasks.
body_text: Why are Keyboard Shortcuts Essential in Revit? Keyboard shortcuts become increasingly valuable as projects grow in size and complexity. Instead of repeatedly navigating through menus, they allow architects to focus on designing, reviewing, and coordinating models more efficiently. Faster BIM Workflow Frequently used commands such as Move, Copy, Align, and Trim can be accessed instantly, helping you complete routine tasks without interrupting your BIM workflow or switching between multiple toolbars. Quicker Construction Documentation Preparing drawings involves repeated actions like placing dimensions, creating detail lines, and managing views. Using Revit shortcuts reduces the time spent on repetitive tasks while making construction documentation easier to update as the model changes. Better Project Coordination Large BIM projects require architects to review linked models, visibility settings, and design revisions regularly. Shortcuts help you navigate between views and coordination tools more quickly, improving project coordination across disciplines. Improved Modelling Efficiency Searching through ribbons and menus breaks concentration, especially when making frequent edits. Keyboard shortcuts keep your focus on the model, allowing you to make changes more quickly and maintain a smoother design process. Greater Productivity Over Time As commonly used shortcuts become second nature, everyday tasks require less effort. This allows architects to spend more time refining designs and solving project challenges instead of navigating the software interface. What are the 50 Most Useful Revit Shortcuts? Learning the right shortcuts can make everyday modelling, editing, and documentation much faster. The commands below are grouped by task, making them easier to remember and apply while working on digital construction projects and improving overall BIM productivity. Category Shortcut Command Purpose Navigation ZF Zoom to Fit Displays the entire model in the active view. ZE Zoom Extents Fits all visible elements within the view. ZZ Zoom Window Zooms into a selected area. WT Tile Windows Displays multiple project views side by side. F8 Orthographic/3D Toggle Switches between orthographic and perspective views. SH Wheel (Pan) Activates pan while navigating the model. Modify MV Move Moves selected elements. CO Copy Creates copies of selected elements. RO Rotate Rotates selected objects. AL Align Aligns elements accurately. TR Trim/Extend Trims or extends elements to a corner. OF Offset Creates a parallel copy at a specified distance. MM Mirror – Pick Axis Mirrors elements about a selected axis. DM Mirror – Draw Axis Mirrors elements using a drawn axis. SC Scale Resizes selected elements proportionally. AR Array Creates multiple copies in a pattern. Model WA Wall Start the Wall tool. DR Door Place doors. WN Window Place windows. RP Reference Plane Creates a reference plane. RL Reference Line Creates a reference line. CM Component Places loadable families. GR Grid Creates structural or architectural grids. LL Level Creates building levels. Annotate DI Aligned Dimension Place dimensions. TG Tag by Category Adds tags to model elements. DL Detail Line Draws 2D detail lines. TX Text Inserts text notes. RM Room Place room objects. RT Room Tag Adds room tags. View VG Visibility/Graphics Controls visibility settings. TL Thin Lines Toggles thin line display. BX Section Box Enables or edits a section box in 3D. HI Hide in View Hides selected elements. HR Reset Temporary Hide/Isolate Restores hidden elements. RH Reveal Hidden Elements Displays hidden objects. Manage UN Undo Reverses the previous action. RE Reload Latest Updates changes from the central model. PU Purge Unused Removes unused project content. KS Keyboard Shortcuts Open the shortcut editor. SN Snaps Controls snapping behaviour. UC Project Units Open unit settings. Collaborate SW Switch Windows Switches between open Revit windows. CS Create Similar Creates another instance of the selected element. EH Hide Element Temporarily hides selected elements. HH Hide Category Hides an entire category in the current view. IC Interference Check Checks for clashes between elements. RL Reload Links Updates linked models. Miscellaneous PR Properties Activates the Properties palette. PB Project Browser Opens or focuses on the Project Browser. F1 Help Opens Revit Help. ESC Cancel Cancels the current command or deselects elements. CTRL + S Save Saves the current project. CTRL + Z Undo Reverses the previous action. Which Shortcut Combinations Save the Most Time? Some Revit commands are even more effective when used together. These combinations reduce repetitive actions, improve design efficiency, and help strengthen your BIM skills while working on projects in modern construction technology. Workflow Shortcut Combination How It Helps Copy and Position Elements CO → AL Copy an element and align it precisely without making manual adjustments. Move and Rotate Objects MV → RO Reposition elements and set the correct orientation in one smooth workflow. Create Walls Efficiently WA → TR → AL Draw walls, clean up intersections, and align them accurately. Add Doors and Windows DR → WN → AL Place openings and align them correctly within walls. Speed Up Documentation DI → TG → TX Add dimensions, tags, and notes quickly while preparing drawings. Edit Similar Elements CS → MV → CO Create similar components, reposition them, and duplicate where required. Review Model Visibility VG → TL → ZZ Adjust visibility settings, switch to thin lines, and zoom into detailed areas. Coordinate Linked Models WT → VG → IC View multiple windows, control visibility, and perform interference checks during coordination. Manage Project Revisions EH → RH → HR Hide elements temporarily, review hidden objects, and restore the original view when finished. Save and Continue Working Ctrl + S → UN Save your progress regularly and undo recent actions safely whenever needed. How Can You Create and Customise Revit Keyboard Shortcuts? Autodesk Revit allows you to customise keyboard shortcuts, making it easier to access the commands you use most often during architectural design. A personalised setup can improve efficiency and create a smoother experience while working with BIM software . Open the Keyboard Shortcuts Menu: Go to View → User Interface → Keyboard Shortcuts, or press KS to open the shortcut manager in Autodesk Revit. Search for a Command: Use the search bar to quickly find the tool or command you want to customise instead of browsing through the full list. Assign a New Shortcut: Enter your preferred key combination in the Press New Keys field and click Assign, ensuring it does not conflict with another command. Edit or Remove Existing Shortcuts: Replace shortcuts that you rarely use or remove them completely to keep your workflow organised Use Consistent Shortcuts: Create logical key combinations that are easy to remember, helping you work faster and switch between commands with minimal interruption. How Can You Become Faster in Revit? Knowing keyboard shortcuts is a great start, but becoming efficient in Revit also requires hands-on experience with real BIM projects and industry workflows. If you're planning to build long-term architecture careers, learning how professionals use Revit in collaborative environments makes a significant difference. With Novatr's BIM Professional Program , you can: Work on real-world BIM projects that reflect industry practices. Learn from experienced architects and BIM professionals. Build practical skills in Revit, coordination, and documentation. Develop a strong portfolio through project-based learning. Earn an industry-recognised BIM certification that strengthens your profile for BIM and AEC roles.

body_text: Homes.com Report: U.S. Home Prices Edge Higher in June as Supply and Demand Trends Remain in Balance July 14, 2026 PDF Version National price growth remained modest as rising sales and inventory point to a more balanced housing market despite differing conditions across local markets. ARLINGTON, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 14, 2026-- Homes.com , a CoStar Group (NASDAQ: CSGP) leading online residential marketplace, released its June 2026 housing market report showing that the national median sale price rose to $401,000, up 1.5% from a year earlier. Home sales increased 6.1% year over year, while active listings were 4.2% higher than a year ago, indicating that both demand and supply continued to expand at a measured pace. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260714498421/en/ United States Sale Prices Key Indicators June Taken together, these trends point to a housing market that is more balanced than in recent years, with neither buyers nor sellers dominating at the national level. Price growth remained modest even as sales activity improved and inventory levels increased, reinforcing the sense of equilibrium across the broader market. Market conditions vary across major metros and property types Even with steady national signals, conditions differed across major housing markets. Some large metros, such as Chicago and Jacksonville, posted solid year-over-year price gains, while others showed flat or declining prices—with San Jose and Seattle posting the largest price drops of 4.6% and 3.1% respectively. Of the 933 markets nationwide tracked by Homes.com, 64% showed year-over-year gains in median sale price while 36% showed price declines. Inventory trends also diverged, with some markets experiencing notable increases in listings while others remained relatively constrained. Differences were also evident across property types. Prices for single-family homes rose more quicker than the overall market, while townhomes and condos saw more modest gains. Inventory increases were generally stronger for single-family homes than for other segments, suggesting that conditions can vary not only by location, but also by property type within the same broader market. “The June data indicate that the housing market is operating on a more even footing overall,” said Brad Case, Homes.com Chief Residential Economist. “While national trends suggest a balance between buyers and sellers, local conditions vary widely, with some markets tilting toward tighter supply and others offering more negotiating room.” Overall, June 2026 reflected a housing market defined by steady national performance and a growing range of local outcomes, as both supply and demand continued to adjust and align more closely. body_text: NEWS EVENTS July 9, 2026 Deployment of Agilysys hospitality technology innovations spanning PMS, POS, retail and booking solutions supports refined guest experiences at the iconic Virginia destination ALPHARETTA, GA (July 9, 2026) – Agilysys, Inc. (Nasdaq: AGYS), a global hospitality-focused technology and services provider, today announced that The Inn at Little Washington, the internationally acclaimed luxury five-star hotel in Virginia’s Shenandoah Valley, has selected a comprehensive suite of Agilysys hospitality solutions to support its dining, lodging and retail operations. For more than four decades, The Inn at Little Washington has drawn guests from across the country and around the world for its Michelin-recognized cuisine, distinctive accommodation and highly orchestrated approach to hospitality. With 24 guest rooms and suites set within a collection of historic buildings, The Inn has built a reputation for delivering immersive, artful experiences where every detail is considered. “Transitioning our core systems across dining and lodging was an important step for The Inn,” said Vincent Ward, Assistant General Manager, from The Inn at Little Washington. “We pride ourselves on delivering world class hospitality to all our guests and wanted our technology to support that mission. Agilysys provided a unified platform that supports our team in delivering a seamless and curated experience.” The Inn selected Agilysys Versa PMS, Agilysys Book, Agilysys Digital Marketing, Agilysys InfoGenesis POS and related solutions to create an integrated environment spanning property management, amenities and food and beverage. Rather than implementing isolated systems, the property adopted a cohesive ecosystem designed to support its standards consistently across departments. title: From Advertising To Client Management: How Agencies Use a White-Label AI Marketing Platform in 2026
summary: From Advertising To Client Management: How Agencies Use a White-Label AI Marketing Platform in 2026 by Logan Welbaum
body_text: Running a marketing agency in 2026 is genuinely hard work. One day you're buried in ad creative, the next you're chasing client approvals, rebuilding a report that somehow broke, and answering the same question you answered last week. Meanwhile, new business doesn't prospect itself. The bigger your client roster gets, the more everything starts feeling like controlled chaos, and the systems that worked for five clients absolutely fall apart at fifteen. A white-label AI marketing platform lets you stop patching things together and actually run a proper operation, under your own brand, without building a single line of software yourself. The Real Challenges Agencies Face When Managing Multiple Client Brands No two clients are the same, and that's exactly what makes agency work so demanding. Different budgets, different target audiences, different approval processes, and wildly different expectations, all happening at once. Teams end up switching between accounts constantly, losing focus, and burning hours just staying organized. Most agencies try to fix this by stacking tools on top of tools. One platform for ads, another for social, another for reporting, another for client communication. It works until it doesn't. Data ends up scattered, things slip through the cracks, and the team spends more time managing the system than actually doing the work. Simplify Advertising Management Across Multiple Channels If your team is logging into Google Ads, then Meta Business Suite, then LinkedIn Campaign Manager, then TikTok, just to check on the same client's campaigns, that's a problem. Not because the platforms are bad, but because that constant switching destroys focus and eats time that should go toward strategy. A professional platform offers white-label marketing tools and brings every major advertising channel under one roof. Your team launches, monitors, and adjusts campaigns from a single dashboard without the tab chaos. The built-in automation handles repetitive optimization work like bid adjustments and creative testing, which means your people spend their time thinking about direction rather than clicking through menus all day. Make Social Media Management Faster and More Consistent Social media management quietly becomes one of the most time-consuming parts of agency work. Writing captions, sourcing visuals, maintaining different brand voices across multiple clients, scheduling everything correctly, and making sure nothing goes out at the wrong time- it adds up fast. Multiply that across ten or fifteen clients, and it starts consuming entire days. A white-label platform changes the workflow significantly. You can build content calendars weeks ahead, generate post ideas using AI, and schedule everything in bulk without treating each piece of content like it's starting from zero. Quality stays consistent, posting stays on schedule, and your team isn't grinding through social content until late evening. Deliver a Better Client Experience With Branded Workspaces Clients notice more than agencies give them credit for. When they're logging into three different tools, receiving reports in random formats, and emailing back and forth just to get a simple update, it feels disorganized, even when the underlying work is solid. A branded client workspace fixes that perception problem entirely. Clients log into something that carries your agency's name and look, not a generic third-party dashboard. From there, they can check campaign performance, approve creative assets, pull reports, and stay informed without needing to contact your team every single time. That level of professionalism builds genuine confidence and, more importantly, it keeps clients from looking elsewhere. Automate Reporting and Save Valuable Time Ask any account manager what they dread most, and reporting usually comes up fast. Pulling numbers from five different platforms, formatting everything into something readable, double-checking figures, and then spending an hour on a call explaining it, every single month. It is a significant time drain that grows heavier as the client list expands. Automated reporting removes most of that burden. Real-time dashboards give clients direct access to their numbers whenever they want them, without anyone on your team having to prepare anything manually. Reports are clean, consistent, and always current. Your team gets those hours back, errors go down, and clients feel better informed, which is genuinely good for the relationship. Create New Revenue Streams Through SaaS and Automated Billing The traditional agency model has a real ceiling. More revenue usually means more clients, which means more staff, more overhead, and more complexity. Growth starts feeling less like success and more like a treadmill. A white-label platform introduces a different path: recurring software revenue. You package the platform under your brand, build your own subscription tiers, and charge clients a monthly fee for access. You can also collect a percentage of ad spend on top of that. Clients get genuinely useful tools, and your agency builds predictable monthly income that doesn't disappear when a project ends. Over time, that recurring base makes the whole business more stable and far easier to scale without proportional cost increases. Features Offered by Plai to Complement Your Agency's White-Label Services Plai is built with agencies in mind, and the feature set reflects that practically. You get a single admin dashboard covering all your clients and brands, custom domain hosting so everything lives under your name, and dedicated client portals for approvals and day-to-day account management. On the advertising side, Plai supports Meta Ads across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp, plus full Google Ads campaign management. Additional tools include GoHighLevel integration, AI UGC avatars for video ad creation, a Smart Creative Builder for generating multiple ad variations, reusable templates, LinkBridge for secure client account access, Stripe integration for automated billing, and localization across forty-plus languages for agencies serving international clients. Why Agencies Should Choose Plai Choosing a white-label platform in 2026 is a real commitment, so the decision deserves careful thought. Plai earns it by offering something most alternatives don't: a genuinely complete platform rather than a collection of loosely connected features. There is no need to hire developers, manage hosting, or stitch together separate tools for advertising, social, reporting, and billing. Everything works together from day one. More importantly, Plai AI is designed around how agencies actually operate, not how a software company imagines they do. The onboarding is straightforward, the branding customization is deep, and the support infrastructure means you are not troubleshooting alone when something needs attention. For agencies serious about scaling, Plai is a practical foundation rather than just another subscription. Frequently Asked Questions What Is a White-Label AI Marketing Platform? A white-label AI marketing platform is a fully built marketing technology product that agencies license and rebrand as their own. The software provider handles all the development, hosting, and technical maintenance. The agency focuses entirely on its clients, its brand, and its growth. From the client's perspective, they are using the agency's platform, not a third-party tool. Can Agencies Generate Recurring Revenue With a White-Label Platform? Absolutely. One of the strongest business cases for adopting a white-label platform is the shift from purely service-based income toward recurring subscription revenue. Agencies can create tiered plans, set their own monthly fees, and charge clients for platform access independently of campaign work. How Does a White-Label Platform Improve Client Management? Client management becomes significantly cleaner when everything lives in one place. Instead of scattered email threads, mismatched reports, and clients logging into unfamiliar third-party dashboards, a white-label platform centralizes the entire relationship. Campaigns, creative approvals, performance data, billing, and communication all sit inside a branded workspace that feels intentional and professional. ‍

title: Phathom Pharmaceuticals to Report Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provide Business Update on Thursday, July 30, 2026
summary: Management to host conference call on Thursday, July 30, 2026, at 8:00 am EDT...
body_text: FLORHAM PARK, N.J., July 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Phathom Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: PHAT), a biopharmaceutical company focused on commercializing and developing novel treatments for gastrointestinal (GI) diseases, today announced that it will host a live webcast at 8:00 am EDT on Thursday, July 30, 2026, to report its second quarter 2026 financial results and provide a business update. A live webcast and additional information about the presentation can be accessed on the Events & Presentations section of the Phathom website at https://investors.phathompharma.com/news-events/events-and-presentations . A recording will be available for 90 days following the conclusion of the call. About Phathom Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Phathom Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of novel treatments for gastrointestinal diseases. Phathom has in-licensed the exclusive rights to vonoprazan, a first-in-class potassium-competitive acid blocker (PCAB), for the U.S., Europe and Canada. Phathom currently markets vonoprazan in the United States as VOQUEZNA® (vonoprazan) tablets for the relief of heartburn associated with Non-Erosive GERD in adults, the healing and maintenance of healing of Erosive GERD in adults and relief of associated heartburn, and as part of VOQUEZNA® TRIPLE PAK® (vonoprazan tablets, amoxicillin capsules, clarithromycin tablets) and VOQUEZNA® DUAL PAK® (vonoprazan tablets, amoxicillin capsules) for the treatment of H. pylori infection in adults. For more information about Phathom, visit the company’s website at www.phathompharma.com and follow on LinkedIn and X .
